result.summary: This PR replaces the existing cross-compiled FreeBSD/NetBSD/OpenBSD CI jobs with jobs that build and run the full test suite natively inside vmactions-provided BSD virtual machines. It reuses the existing host-mode CI driver, adds new 00_setup_env_*_native.sh environment files, and removes the old cross-compile-only env files and workflow entries. It also includes two small functional-test fixes (an lsof warning suppression for FreeBSD, and a bounded REST client timeout) needed to get tests passing under the new jobs, and excludes two flaky/slow tests (feature_reindex_init, p2p_private_broadcast_retry_v1) from the BSD runs.
result.problem: BSD binaries are currently cross-compiled in CI but never executed, so regressions that only manifest on BSD are caught in third-party nightly builds well after merge and require separate fixup PRs (cited examples: #36078, #36145). This is felt by BSD-cross-compile maintainers and by whoever has to write the delayed fixups.

open_concerns: maflcko: the vmactions BSD VMs (especially OpenBSD and NetBSD) have a meaningfully high nightly failure rate in hebasto's tracking repo; adding them to the PR hot path risks normalizing ignored/red CI unless someone commits to triaging intermittent failures, and the motivating regressions (#36078/#36145) are NetBSD/OpenBSD-specific where flakiness is worst.
maflcko: questions whether maintaining these jobs costs more than periodically porting fixups from nightly builds.
Unresolved: whether to merge all three BSDs or start with FreeBSD only, given FreeBSD showed zero nightly failures in the sampled month versus OpenBSD's high failure rate.

categories.name: build
categories.evidence: Primary subject: replaces BSD cross-compile CI jobs with native VM-based build-and-test jobs, touching ci.yml, ci/README.md, and multiple ci/test/00_setup_env_*.sh files.
categories.rationale: Addresses real but narrow BSD cross-compile regressions currently caught only in third-party nightly builds ('recent examples include #36078 and #36145' per description), which is a genuine but secondary-platform pain point. The value is contested: maflcko argues added VM flakiness (up to 19/33 nightly failures on OpenBSD in one month) could offset the benefit, so this sits below the top of the build priority ladder which favors release integrity and mainstream supported-platform breakage over niche cross-compile targets.

result.card: Adds native FreeBSD/NetBSD/OpenBSD CI jobs (via vmactions VMs) that build and run the full test suite, replacing the current cross-compile-only BSD jobs that never execute the binaries. The stated problem is that BSD regressions are currently caught only in third-party nightly builds and fixed after the fact (citing merged fixups #36078 and #36145). Reviewer maflcko raises a substantive, evidenced objection that these VMs (especially OpenBSD, and to a lesser extent NetBSD) have shown high nightly failure rates and could degrade trust in CI more than the benefit of catching BSD regressions early; hebasto gives a narrower concept ACK favoring a FreeBSD-only start. The author has posted a 90-day flake-rate analysis (~2.2%) but the debate is unresolved, and the author says they may close the PR if no further input arrives. The PR is in draft, needs a rebase, and conflicts with several other open CI PRs.
